context: During cooling, a significant increase of IF below ∼620K is found, Fig. 3a, which was never observed during similar experiments on severely deformed paramagnetic metals such as Cu, Ti, Mg and Al [23,26]. This behavior is associated with a magnetomechanical contribution, i.e. the dissipation of energy of the mechanical vibrations due to motion of magnetic domain walls, which increases the total damping in Ni at temperatures below the Curie temperature. The heat flow data (the right ordinate in Fig. 4) show the Curie temperature around 628K . In ECAP-processed Ni, the magnetomechanical damping is strongly inhibited by SPD due to high local residual stresses and due to the presence of extra free volume at GBs that suppress the motion of magnetic domain walls [17]. After recrystallization during the first TDIF run to 873K , the magnetomechanical damping becomes pronounced below the Curie point. To avoid its influence on the above estimates of the activation parameters of the high-temperature IF background above the Curie point, all temperaturedependent IF curves measured during the second run were shifted to the same value at 573K as shown in Fig. 3b.
